findings.title: Error details mismatched to IDs via zip with dict values
findings.body: fetch_error_details builds node_ids from error_ids, calls nodestore.backend.get_multi which returns a dict keyed by node id, then does zip(error_ids, events.values()). Dict value order is not guaranteed to correspond to error_ids order, and missing keys shift alignment. As a result an ErrorEvent can get the wrong id/title/message/timestamp, producing incorrect error context in the Seer summary request.

findings.title: Mutual-exclusion validation uses truthiness instead of presence
findings.body: validate_timestamp checks self.initial_data.get("age") and validate_age checks self.initial_data.get("timestamp"). Falsy values like age=0 or timestamp=0 therefore do not trigger the error, even though both fields would be present. Since timestamp explicitly allows min_value=0, a report with timestamp=0 and age set would incorrectly pass validation. The check should test key presence, e.g. "age" in self.initial_data.

findings.title: Merged-PR template calls truncate helper on wrong class
findings.body: CommitContextIntegration defines _truncate_title, but get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title). Unless PRCommentWorkflow also defines that helper, this raises AttributeError at comment-render time, breaking merged-PR suspect-issue comments for GitHub and GitLab which were just switched to this helper.

findings.title: Detector update reads wrong validated key for type
findings.body: update() does validated_data.get("detector_type", instance.group_type).slug while create() and validate_type use the field named "type" (validated_data["type"]). validated_data will therefore never contain "detector_type", so type changes on update are silently ignored and the detector keeps its old type.

findings.title: Flag-gated table visualization discards real data
findings.body: When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization, tableResultComponent renders <TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} /> instead of using result.data/result.meta, eventView, fieldAliases and renderers computed just above. This ships an always-empty table behind the flag, losing all query results.

findings.title: Column fallback crashes when meta.fields is missing
findings.body: The fallback columnOrder does Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields). Optional chaining only guards tableData and meta, not fields: if tableData or meta is undefined, Object.keys(undefined) throws TypeError and the whole widget crashes. It should default to {} or [] before calling Object.keys.
